problem: Given that $y=2{x}^{3}-2x$ for $x=x(t),$ and that $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}=1$ at the point where $x=-2,$ find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}.$
worked_solution:
Differentiating the given relation with respect to $t$ using implicit differentiation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =2{x}^{3}-2x \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{x}^{3}-2x) \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2{x}^{3}-2x) \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot (6{x}^{2}-2).\end{aligned}
$$

Now we can substitute the given information $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}=1$ and $x=-2,$ and solve for $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =1\cdot (6\cdot (-2)^{2}-2)=22.\end{aligned}
$$
